# Example data: fisher generalized spatial mark-resight, western Oregon Cascades

**These data are SIMULATED.** They were generated by the module's own
simulator with known parameter values, then written in the file formats a
field crew would really produce. Because the truth is known, the worked
example (WALKTHROUGH.md; Appendix S1) can show whether the analysis recovers
it. Fisher names, dates, photo file names, sexes, body masses, elevations and
GPS HDOP values are decoration added for realism; the model does not use them.

## The (simulated) study

Fishers (*Pekania pennanti*) are mid-sized forest carnivores. A team wants to
know how many fishers live in a block of managed forest in the western Oregon
Cascades (UTM zone 10N), and whether more of them live where the canopy is
dense.

- **Marking (May 2025).** 25 Tomahawk box traps on a 5 x 5 grid, 1.5 km
  apart, run for 5 nights (12-16 May). Every fisher caught got coloured,
  numbered ear tags. 23 different fishers were caught (57 captures). 9 of them
  also got GPS collars.
- **Resighting (June-August 2025).** 49 baited trail cameras on a 7 x 7 grid,
  1.5 km apart, run for 10 weeks from 2 June. The box-trap grid sits in the
  middle of the camera grid. Each independent photo event of a fisher was
  scored as "ear-tag read" (the fisher is identified), "ear-tag, number
  unreadable" (tagged, identity unknown) or "no tag".
- **GPS.** The 9 collared fishers gave 30 fixes each (270 fixes), one about
  every two days. They are thinned enough to treat as independent.
- **Habitat.** A 500 m grid covering the cameras plus a 4 km buffer
  (1,156 pixels, 289 km2) with percent canopy cover.

Because the tagged fishers were caught at traps in the middle of the study
area, they are **not** a random sample of the population. The marking
process has to be modelled: a generalized spatial mark-resight (gSMR) model
(Whittington et al. 2018).

## Design dimensions

| dimension | value |
|---|---|
| cameras | 49 (7 x 7, 1,500 m spacing); 24 on trails or skid roads, 25 off-trail |
| resighting occasions | 10 weeks; 3 cameras failed part-way (`weeks_active`) |
| marking traps | 25 box traps (5 x 5, 1,500 m spacing, centred in the camera grid) |
| marking occasions | 5 trap nights |
| marked (tagged) fishers | 23 |
| GPS-collared fishers | 9 (30 fixes each) |
| photo events | 360: 194 "ear-tag read", 54 "ear-tag, number unreadable", 112 "no tag" |
| state space | 1,156 pixels of 500 m, 289 km2 (cameras + 4 km) |
| camera covariate | `on_trail` (0/1) |
| density covariate | `canopy_cover_pct` (mean ~50%, SD ~12%) |

## Files and columns

**cameras.csv** (49 rows, one per camera)
- `camera_id`: camera name (FC01-FC49).
- `utm_e`, `utm_n`: UTM zone 10N coordinates (m).
- `on_trail`: 1 = camera on a trail or skid road, 0 = off-trail bait tree.
- `weeks_active`: 10 characters, one per week; 1 = camera working, 0 = not.
- `bait`, `notes`: field notes (not used).

**fisher_photos.csv** (360 rows, one per independent photo event)
- `camera_id`: camera that took the photo.
- `week`: resighting week (1-10).
- `date`: date of the photo (not used).
- `tag_status`: "ear-tag read", "ear-tag, number unreadable" or "no tag".
- `fisher_id`: ear-tag ID when read (FI-001 ...); blank otherwise.
- `photo`: image file name (not used).

**box_traps.csv** (25 rows)
- `trap_id` (BX01-BX25), `utm_e`, `utm_n`, `trap_type` (not used).

**box_trap_captures.csv** (57 rows, one per capture)
- `fisher_id`: ear-tag ID given at first capture.
- `night`: trap night (1-5); `date` (not used).
- `trap_id`: box trap where the fisher was caught.
- `sex`, `new_capture`, `mass_kg`: handling data (not used).

**gps_fixes.csv** (270 rows)
- `fisher_id`, `fix_time`, `utm_e`, `utm_n`, `hdop` (HDOP not used).

**habitat_grid.csv** (1,156 rows, one per 500 m pixel)
- `x`, `y`: pixel centre (UTM zone 10N, m).
- `canopy_cover_pct`: canopy cover (%), the density covariate.
- `elevation_m`: not used.
- `habitat`: 1 = habitat (all pixels here).

`config.yaml` maps these columns to the module.

## TRUE values (simulated)

Generated by `dev/scr-smr/make_example.R` (seed 2025 for the population and
detections; seed 7 for the decorative fields). Truth object:
`dev/scr-smr/example_truth.rds`.

| quantity | true value |
|---|---|
| expected density at average canopy cover | 0.25 fishers per km2 (about 73 expected in 289 km2) |
| **realised abundance in the state space, N** | **86 fishers** |
| **realised density** | **0.298 fishers per km2** (86 / 289 km2) |
| realised marked fraction | 0.267 (23 / 86) |
| sigma (spatial scale of movement) | 1,000 m |
| 95% home-range area (circular) | 18.8 km2 |
| resight rate lambda0 (off-trail camera at the activity centre) | 0.30 photo events per week |
| on-trail effect on resight rate (log scale) | 0.70 (rate ratio 2.0) |
| P(ear-tag number readable), delta | 0.80 |
| nightly box-trap capture probability at the activity centre, pm0 | 0.30 |
| canopy effect on density (log scale, per SD of canopy cover) | 0.50 (rate ratio 1.65) |

The realised population (86) is above the expected 73. That is chance, not
an error: N is a Poisson draw around the expected value.
